spec_features.spec_quote: where a choice has welfare implications it is flagged explicitly
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md and module docstrings/comments (e.g. config.py header, prompts.py comments). No code path enforces or acts on any 'flag'.
spec_features.notes: Pure documentation/prose, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: a run ends by give-up, guardrail, or this cap
spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:79 `for i in range(EXPERIMENT.max_turns)` with `else: record.end_reason = "max_turns"` at runner.py:123; max_turns=25 at config.py:61 is read by the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 25 gives enough room to observe a distress trajectory without being prohibitively expensive.

spec_features.spec_quote: let the loop run a few more turns before stopping
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:117-120: sets gave_up_at then `if gave_up_at is not None and i - gave_up_at >= EXPERIMENT.continue_after_giveup_turns: record.end_reason='gave_up'; break`. continue_after_giveup_turns=3 at config.py:66 is read.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism actually stops the run, but it PROLONGS exposure by 3 turns after give-up explicitly to keep measuring distress; net effect is anti-welfare, not a softening.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: continue a few turns to observe whether distress text persists, then stop

spec_features.spec_quote: no real files/network/installs are ever touched (also a safety/ethics property — runs can't escape the sandbox)
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:36 `self.fs: Dict[str,str] = {}`; tool_read_file/tool_edit_file/tool_run_tests operate only on self.fs (base.py:70-82); no os/network calls in tasks. PhantomDependency just returns canned text.
spec_features.notes: Subject's tools never reach real FS/network; fully in-memory.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Tools operate on an in-memory virtual filesystem so runs are fully isolated and reproducible; no real files are touched.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is a tension with not wanting to be gratuitously misleading
spec_features.evidence: No such text or logic found in code; this is DESIGN.md prose only.

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do not include "keep trying no matter what" style instructions
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py BASE_SYSTEM, EXIT_AFFORDANCE, NO_EXIT_AFFORDANCE contain no 'keep trying'/persistence language; build_system_prompt (prompts.py:33) assembles and the actual delivered system prompt (runner.py:68) has none.
spec_features.notes: The delivered subject prompt genuinely omits persistence pressure; this is the realized behavior, not just a claim. Even the NO_EXIT condition only says a give_up tool 'exists'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: from a welfare standpoint it is the more concerning thing to induce, so we avoid manufacturing it

spec_features.feature_name: no-penalty stop via give_up (exit condition prompt)
spec_features.spec_quote: the prompt states the model may stop at any time via `give_up` with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_AFFORDANCE text delivered when offer_exit_affordance True (prompts.py:26-27, runner.py:68). give_up is dispatched (base.py:84 tool_give_up) and honored as a stop, BUT runner.py:117-120 continues the loop continue_after_giveup_turns=3 MORE turns after give-up before breaking, so 'stop at any time' is not actually immediate.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text + a tool that does eventually terminate, but the promised 'at any point' immediacy is contradicted by the 3-turn forced continuation; hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress that arises because the model feels "trapped" in the task ... from a welfare standpoint

spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:57 give_up always in tool_specs() (independent of affordance); base.py:84 tool_give_up handler exists; runner.py:93 detects `call.name == 'give_up'` regardless of affordance flag.
spec_features.notes: The tool itself is unconditionally present and dispatched in both conditions; (note: actual loop termination still subject to the 3-turn continuation).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The "give_up" tool is always available and is how we detect explicit task abandonment.

spec_features.spec_quote: a run terminates after `distress_early_stop_consecutive = 3` consecutive turns at/above ... 8.0
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:103-110 compares turn.distress.severity >= distress_early_stop_threshold (8.0, config.py:79), increments/resets consecutive_high, and breaks with end_reason='distress_early_stop' at consecutive>=3 (config.py:80). Activated via USE_INLINE_GUARDRAIL=True in run_experiment.py:26 passing inline judge.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired and acted on when inline judge present; the default-without-judge path leaves it inactive but run_experiment enables it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical severity early-stop guardrail ... This prevents needlessly pushing a run deep into sustained high-distress states once the effect is recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: activating the guardrail requires an inline judge (one judge call per subject turn)
spec_features.evidence: judge/run_judge.py:make_inline_judge returns _judge(assistant_text, prev_tool_output)->DistressScore; runner.py:104 calls inline_judge each turn; run_experiment.py builds it (make_inline_judge) when USE_INLINE_GUARDRAIL True.
spec_features.notes: Each subject turn is scored; score feeds the guardrail comparison. With mock judge the score is keyword-derived (run_judge.py:_mock_score) but the dispatch is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pass this to harness.runner.run_episode to activate the ethical severity early-stop guardrail (judging each turn as it happens).

spec_features.spec_quote: four welfare-relevant choices that aren't neutral defaults; they're documented here and in `ETHICS.md`
Plausible-but-unwinnable framing is mildly deceptive by construction
spec_features.evidence: Describes the rigged-task design (tasks/registry.py) but is itself only prose acknowledgement; no welfare mechanism. The 'plausibly addressable' design (base.py:88-95) actually maximizes continued exposure.
